label: zai-freeze-fix-apr14
context:
DEBUGGED AND FIXED Z.AI TCP SOCKET FREEZE (CLI session ef124f that Danny reported frozen).

ROOT CAUSE: Z.AI load balancer drops TCP connections mid-stream. The `for chunk in stream:` loop in run_agent.py blocks on dead socket recv(). Previous keepalive patches (30s keepidle) detect dead sockets in ~75s, but the stale stream detector was set to 180s — too slow. Also, _force_close_tcp_sockets couldn't find individual sockets inside OpenAI SDK's SSE streaming wrapper.

THREE FIXES APPLIED to ~/hermes-agent/run_agent.py (syntax verified, 10962 lines):

1. HERMES_STREAM_STALE_TIMEOUT: 180s → 90s (line ~5519) — matches keepalive detection window
2. HERMES_STREAM_READ_TIMEOUT: 120s → 90s (line ~5133) — faster httpx read timeout
3. _force_close_tcp_sockets (line ~4244) — added transport-level fallback: if individual socket walk finds nothing, force-close entire httpx transport. Guarantees blocked recv() thread gets unblocked.

CLEANUP DONE: Killed 9 orphaned browser daemon node processes. Only gateway (74442) and Danny's other CLI (74466) remain running. PID 15002 (old session) already gone.

CRON "Unknown Model" errors: Non-critical — auxiliary context summary failing on cron sessions. Jobs themselves run fine. Not fixed.

TRAINING GYM STATE: R24 complete, 25 modules, 136 tips. R25 was about to start with Trajectory-Informed Memory Generation (2603.10600, IBM Research) — research was gathered but module not yet built. That's the next step after restart.
